newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by outlooks for another day of light marketings following slow receipts on Monday, livestock dealers said.

Lower prices Friday and Monday reportedly spurred lighter marketings as farmers held back some hogs, they said. USDA interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs Monday had a top of $57.00, down $1.50 since Thursday.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant on Tuesday were seen $57.00 to $57.50, the dealers said.
Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant could range $57.00 to $57.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices were seen $57.50 to $58.00, they said.

Cash hog prices also were seen firm amid moderate demand from packers for live inventory despite continued reduced operating hours because of unprofitable operating margins, the dealers said. Packer operating margins reportedly were $10.00 to $12.00 per head in the red, they said.
Hog slaughter on Monday was estimated at 285,000 head, compared with 305,000 a week ago and 307,000 a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
